findings.comment: review-r1 SP1 (spec, probed: False); files docs/ci-runner.md:80, .github/workflows/ci.yml:31-34, scripts/ci/guest-provision.sh
findings.text: The acceptance item 'fork code cannot reach pc1' (user: 'no other external commits, only us') rests on a procedural writer rule. Nothing enforces it. Repro: An admin (an org member) opens a PR from outsider:branch into wave/*. Org members need no approval under all_external_contributors, and the merge commit's ci.yml (which the fork can strip of the guard and tests/ci/) runs on the persistent pc1 runner. After that review the outsider can still push to the head, and nobody has verified whether GitHub gates those synchronize runs. The docs omit this. Fix: Make guest-provision.sh install a root-owned job-started hook outside the runner directory, enabled through a root-owned systemd drop-in, that refuses unless GITHUB_EVENT_PATH names this repository, the event is allowed, and a pull_request head is this repository. Add a fake-guest test. The coordinator deploys it and checks live that always() steps do not run after a hook failure. Alternatively, record a user decision narrowing the acceptance; the docs gain the outsider-push case either way.

tests.name: was installed by provision, so these tests run the real thing
lets the job go on for a pull request from this repository, a push to dev and a manual run
ends the job, and its always() steps, for every event that is not this repository's own
refuses a payload it cannot trust: missing, not at the runner's path, a link, stale, empty, not JSON, not an object, with a repeated key
does not read the hook's decision from anything a workflow can set: its own environment, PYTHONPATH, or a planted module
ends the job when its own policy cannot run, instead of letting it go on
fails the hook, without a worker to stop, when it finds no Runner.Worker above it
says why it refused, and writes the reason to a file the next person can read
and its policy carry no write bit for the runner user's group or others

findings.comment: review-r1 SP2 (spec, probed: True); files tests/ci/workflow-admission.test.ts:26, tests/ci/workflow-admission.test.ts:53
findings.text: The admission tests do not model the writer-opened fork PR: every row's github.actor is 'someone'. Repro: Extend the guard with '|| github.actor == "gridshift-admin"' on the fork pull_request clause. bun run --bun test tests/ci/workflow-admission.test.ts still passes 90/90 (P2). Fix: Assert that the job if: names no identity context (actor, triggering_actor, sender, author_association, user.login), or add a fork row whose actor and sender are a member.

findings.comment: review-r1 ST1 (standards, probed: False); files tests/ci/actions-expression.ts:41-58, tests/ci/guard-enforcement.test.ts:34
findings.text: Judgement call: Speculative Generality and Duplicated Code. The evaluator supports functions, indexing and status functions that no job if: uses, while holds() remains a second evaluator. Repro: Reading only: no job-level if: uses contains, startsWith, endsWith, [ ] or the status functions; step ifs go through holds() instead. Fix: Route holds() through runs() with a steps context, or cut the evaluator back to ==, !=, &&, ||, ! and . access.
